assignment: Review GetShiftSummaryAsync and only directly material helper, authorization, DTO, expense writer semantics, and existing test source. Static only; preserve prior reviews.

source.behavior: Looks up the requested shift by ID using AsNoTracking; missing shift throws InvalidOperationException, converted by endpoint to NotFound. Loads names for opener and optional closer, then delegates to BuildShiftSummaryAsync. That helper loads non-cancelled orders for exactly this ShiftId; maps them to domain Orders; computes SalesRules report after identifying cash-on-delivery orders without a Settled DriverCustody; sums all Expense rows carrying this ShiftId; and returns DTO fields including persisted opening/expected/actual/difference snapshots and reason. This is a read projection; it does not recalculate, post, or mutate cash state.

cross_file_evidence.behavior: LoadSalesOrdersAsync excludes Status == nameof(OrderStatus.Cancelled), applies optional business date interval if supplied, and filters by exact ShiftId when nonempty. This summary passes null interval and a shift ID. COD amounts stay in the cash-with-drivers measure until a Settled custody row exists; pending/unsettled COD is excluded from collected cash. The helper documents that settlement shortages are reported separately, not subtracted a second time.
GET /api/reports/shifts/{id} requires RequireReportsAccessAsync; successful lookup returns summary; nonexistent shift maps to 404.

ShiftSummaryDto returns opening cash, nullable expected/actual/difference, SalesReportDto, ExpensesTotalPiastres and operational identity/time/reason. It does not expose each expense's PaymentAccountId/PaidFromDrawer or custody details; field is a shift-associated expense total, not explicitly a drawer-only sum.

Expense creation accepts protected source accounts including drawer or protected main account; requires an existing Open shift, and persists the requested ShiftId, amount and PaymentAccountId on ExpenseEntity while posting a linked treasury movement. Thus BuildShiftSummaryAsync's unqualified ShiftId sum includes expenses sourced from any permitted account, not only drawer cash.

Shift_summary_reports_sales_expenses_and_opening_cash_for_one_shift creates one cash sale and one drawer expense, then asserts opening cash, order count, net sales and expense total. It does not distinguish drawer vs main-account expenses or test stale close snapshots / unsettled COD.

assessment.financial_relevance: High as a manager-facing view of one shift's sales/cash classification, associated expense total, and cash-close snapshot. It does not produce or post the cash difference; close handlers own those stored snapshot values.
observations: Sales rows are shift-scoped and cancelled orders excluded by the shared loader. Unsettled COD is reported outside collected cash; settled custody restores it to collected classification. No counterevidence found in this method path.

ExpensesTotalPiastres includes every Expense with the shift ID, including a protected non-drawer source. This can differ from cash spent from the drawer; DTO/summary call it expenses total and includes no drawer-only label. Treat as a scope/label ambiguity unless the Shifts screen promises drawer cash expenses only. Existing test covers only drawer expense.

Expected/actual/cash difference values are copied from the Shift record. This method does not verify them against a fresh reconciliation; snapshot correctness depends on close workflow and should not be inferred from this read endpoint.

Cross-reference preserved: significant-actions can project an approved expense and its linked treasury movement as two source rows/count entries; this shift summary's Expense total sums only Expense rows and does not sum linked movement too, so that prior presentation duplication does not itself double the expense total here.
counterevidence: The method and DTO consistently scope the sum to expenses associated with the shift; an expense from the main account may still be an operational expense belonging to the shift, so inclusion may be intended.
The source comment describes per-shift sales + expenses + discrepancy; it does not promise drawer-only expenses or recomputation of closed snapshots.
assessment.recommended_validation: If the intended summary contract is drawer-only outflow, add a test with both drawer and main-account expense and specify expected total; if it is all operational expense, label/document that scope. For closed shifts, add close-flow-to-summary assertion that the stored expected/actual/difference snapshot is shown unchanged. No fix recommended from static evidence alone.
